rules.reason: signed-in users manage their own bank accounts, same owner-scoped posture as the rest of finance
an import profile is the user's own how-to-read-my-bank configuration
import runs are historical events: readable and creatable by their owner, never updatable or deletable -- the provenance record for imported evidence must not be rewritable

owners read and import their own statement lines, and UPDATE only to record reconciliation work (match_status/matched_to/resolved_as) -- which is attributed in the change log, so who reconciled what is auditable. No delete: imported evidence is append-only, and the transitions on match_status constrain what an update may do to it
importing a statement is an ordinary operator verb; the object requires a signed-in identity and verifies the bank account belongs to the caller

resolving a line as a fee, interest, transfer or NSF is an ordinary operator verb; the object checks ownership of the line (and of any counterpart account) and composes through the shared journal composer, which is idempotent by provenance

the matcher only ever writes SUGGESTIONS onto the caller's own unmatched lines (and auto-confirms solely at the configured tier), so running it is safe for any signed-in owner as well as the scheduler

page objects are public execute like every other site_* page (see packages/app-finance's site_trial_balance rule); the object itself gates all data on a signed-in identity and scopes every read to the caller's own bank accounts and lines, so an anonymous or cross-owner request never sees another owner's reconciliation
signed-in users manage their own value accounts; managed_by names who runs one day to day but ownership still governs the record itself
the runner only reads bank_lines/payments and creates tasks scoped to the item's own owner (or reconcile.escalate_to), so running it is safe for any signed-in owner as well as the scheduler
same posture as the CSV importer: a signed-in operator verb that verifies the bank account belongs to the caller before reading anything
